item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-b3059b36a855510c","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International reported that Egypt was characterized by widespread violations of its obligations under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, including arbitrary detention, torture, unfair trials, and repression of expression, association, and peaceful assembly.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The submission was published in January–February 2023 and describes ongoing conditions; it is an external institutional finding rather than a dated incident.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns the Egyptian state during Abdel Fattah el-Sisi’s presidency; direct personal authorization is not established by this source.","limitations":["The supplied unit summarizes multiple findings without case-level detail.","The source does not establish which specific officials ordered or implemented each violation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-56352226494fe107","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Mahmoud Hussein was re-arrested on 30 August 2023 after having spent two years in arbitrary pretrial detention for wearing an anti-torture T-shirt; Amnesty reported that he remained detained at Badr 1 prison pending retrial after an allegedly grossly unfair emergency-court conviction and allegations of torture.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The re-arrest and detention occurred during 2023; the source also reports earlier proceedings as context.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to Egyptian detention and judicial institutions under the government led by el-Sisi, not personally to el-Sisi.","limitations":["The source is an Amnesty urgent-action account and does not provide a final judicial determination of the torture allegations.","No evidence is supplied of a presidential order in this individual case."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1cdb9a372cf077b9","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International reported an ongoing human-rights and impunity crisis in Egypt, including entrenched gender-based violence and discrimination against women, girls, and LGBTI people.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The submission was dated 25 January 2023 and describes ongoing conditions relevant to the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns state-wide conditions during el-Sisi’s presidency; the source does not establish his personal involvement in each reported pattern.","limitations":["The supplied unit provides a high-level summary rather than quantified 2023 incidence data.","The source does not distinguish national from subnational responsibility."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1cdb9a372cf077b9","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International reported that Egypt’s legal protections for human rights had regressed since 2013 and that the country experienced widespread violations involving the death penalty, torture, arbitrary deprivation of liberty, and unfair trials.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","4B.2"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The submission was published for the UN Human Rights Committee’s 2023 session and describes a trend extending into the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns the Egyptian state across the post-2013 period, including el-Sisi’s presidency; it does not prove personal authorship of every legal or institutional change.","limitations":["The source summary does not identify individual laws, dates, or implementing agencies.","The causal contribution of el-Sisi personally is not isolated."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cd2ad28b3572d00b","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"On 30 April 2023, Egypt’s House of Representatives approved the articles of a bill regulating possession and breeding of dangerous animals and dogs, licensing non-dangerous dogs, addressing stray animals, and imposing penalties intended to deter conduct and protect public health and citizen safety; final approval was deferred to a later session.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The parliamentary action occurred during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measure was introduced and advanced by parliament; the supplied source does not show el-Sisi’s personal initiation, approval, funding, or implementation.","limitations":["The source reports approval of articles, not final enactment or implementation.","The measure concerns animal-related public safety rather than broad domestic violence outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bf5603126f4ab003","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Egypt ratified the Convention on Nuclear Safety on 25 September 2023, which entered into force for Egypt on 24 December 2023.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.4","1B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Both ratification and entry into force occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The treaty action is attributable to the Egyptian state during el-Sisi’s presidency; the source does not identify the presidential decision process or domestic implementation resources.","limitations":["The source does not show compliance, inspection performance, staffing, or corrective action after ratification."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bf5603126f4ab003","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Egypt had an IAEA safeguards agreement in force in connection with the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons, registered as effective from 30 June 1982.","question_ids":["1B.4","1B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The agreement predates 2023 but remained the applicable safeguards framework during the target period.","ruler_attribution":"This is an inherited state-level institutional arrangement, not evidence of a new el-Sisi decision in 2023.","limitations":["The supplied record does not report 2023 inspections, findings, funding, or compliance disputes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-836c1ac64be5b164","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Egypt convened the Cairo Summit for Peace on 21 October 2023 to address hostilities in Gaza and Israel; the UN Special Coordinator welcomed the effort and recorded calls for a political solution and concern about regional spillover.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","2B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The summit and statement occurred during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The summit was convened by the Egyptian authorities during el-Sisi’s presidency; the source does not attribute the diplomatic initiative solely to el-Sisi personally.","limitations":["Convening a summit does not establish that a durable ceasefire or settlement resulted.","The source reports the UN official’s assessment, not a complete account of Egypt’s negotiating conduct."]},{"source_id":"SRC-836c1ac64be5b164","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Egypt facilitated the entry of the first truckloads of humanitarian aid into Gaza through Rafah during the October 2023 conflict.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","2B.10","3B.9","6B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The aid entry occurred by 21 October 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The action is attributed to Egyptian authorities during el-Sisi’s presidency; the source does not establish the precise presidential order or Egypt’s control over subsequent aid flows.","limitations":["The UN statement expressly said this step needed to be followed by safe and continuous aid, so it does not establish sustained delivery.","The source does not quantify aid volume or humanitarian effect."]},{"source_id":"SRC-246e7ee65d10f833","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Egypt’s 2023 National Child Labour Survey reported 4.2 million working children, including 3.7 million in hazardous or unlawful work.","question_ids":["3B.7","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The quantitative result is explicitly from a 2023 national survey, although the factsheet was published in 2025.","ruler_attribution":"The result describes national conditions during el-Sisi’s presidency; it does not by itself establish presidential responsibility or causation.","limitations":["The supplied source does not provide the survey methodology, comparison baseline, or regional distribution.","The statistic is an outcome indicator and does not show which policies caused it."]},{"source_id":"SRC-246e7ee65d10f833","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The Egyptian government’s 2018–2025 National Action Plan on the worst forms of child labour was reported to have expanded labour inspections, education, economic-empowerment programs, and child-protection measures, while ACCEL Africa training involved more than 2,600 stakeholders and digitalized labour and occupational-safety inspections.","question_ids":["5B.6","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The plan and reported implementation span the target period, but the factsheet was published in 2025 and does not isolate 2023 activities.","ruler_attribution":"The plan was led by the Government of Egypt during el-Sisi’s presidency, with ILO support; the source does not establish his personal management of the programs.","limitations":["The source also reports continuing severe child labour, so these are implementation actions rather than proof of overall success.","The supplied text does not provide budget amounts, geographic coverage, or independent evaluation results."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-742b736f699881d4","SRC-7fed1e2a265685b5","SRC-23342309bb1d97f7","SRC-a3380e1787976cbb","SRC-05ce607987ab7e15"],"batch_limitations":["Several supplied documents contain only webpage navigation or historical/contextual material and provide no concrete 2023 fact relevant to the specified lenses.","The evidence is predominantly institutional reporting and does not establish Abdel Fattah el-Sisi’s personal intent, authorship, or control for most state-level findings.","No scoring is provided."]}
